target_customer: Hosts and attendees of virtual happy hours, networking events and comedy shows; later students (SlaySchool)
problem: Zoom breakout rooms isolate groups, so online social events feel unlike a shared physical space.
business_model: Browser video platform for events (pricing not found); later consumer AI study product

founders.name: Ali Jiwani
founders.background_notes: YC page says he later pivoted to SlaySchool and earlier founded companies in health and food logistics (details not sourced further).

founders.name: Anson Kao
education: University of Waterloo, Mechatronics, class of 2010
founders.background_notes: YC page: 10 years of web development and startup experience in Toronto.

competitors.name: Zoom
competitors.what: General video meetings with breakout rooms

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser based multi party video with tables of up to 35 users per room and audio bleed between nearby tables (TechCrunch 2020-09).

defensibility.rationale: Feature layered on commodity WebRTC video; Zoom and Meet could copy table hopping and many virtual event tools appeared in 2020.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not found whether incumbents copied it; the company moved away from the product (YC page says it pivoted to SlaySchool).

market_need_then: Pandemic lockdowns in 2020 created demand for online social gatherings and Zoom fatigue (TechCrunch 2020-09).

branding.domain_note: Used rally.video, not a .com (TechCrunch 2020-09). The domain now shows an unrelated casino page, so it appears to have lapsed.

rebrands.why: The product pivoted (YC page and TechCrunch Startup Battlefield profile; date not stated)

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with many other companies named Rally, no brand press found, and the product was replaced.

pivots.from: Zoom for social events (began with live comedy events)
pivots.to: SlaySchool, an AI study partner for students
pivots.why: Not stated; TechCrunch profile says it pivoted eight times (secondary listing).

outcome_analysis: Rally launched into the 2020 pandemic demand for online social events and presented at TechCrunch Disrupt Battlefield in September 2020. The product was a thin layer over video that Zoom and Meet could imitate, and the team later pivoted to SlaySchool, which the YC page says has over half a million users. No funding round beyond an unverified small seed figure was found, and the reason for the pivot is not public.
notes: rally.video now serves an unrelated casino page, so the original site is dead. Amy Liu is on the YC page as a founder of Hotpot Studios; another profile lists her as an investor, so she is not recorded as co-founder. An aggregator (Standout) lists about 125K seed funding, unverified, so not recorded as a round. Search results about Rally legal tech (Spellbook) and Rally crypto concern different companies. Failure factor is weak because the company is Active under a pivoted product.
